title: Most Secure Business Email Providers in India (2026): Microsoft 365 vs Google Workspace vs Zoho vs Proton
excerpt: How Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Zoho and Proton compare on encryption, key control, MFA, DMARC, audit logs and data location, with rules for choosing.
body:
"Most secure" depends on the threat you are guarding against. If the worry is a stolen password or a spoofed invoice, the best provider is the one whose admin controls your team will actually switch on. If the worry is the provider itself, or a government request for your data, the answer changes and so do the trade-offs. This guide compares Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Zoho and Proton on the security points that matter to an Indian business, and says plainly where each one is weaker.

A note on sources: TechZoid supplies Microsoft 365 plans and Zoho Mail and Workplace. We do not list Google Workspace or Proton, so statements about them are widely documented general behaviour. Confirm the current position on each provider's own published pages before relying on it.

## Start with the threats, not the brand

Most mailbox incidents in Indian businesses do not involve anyone breaking encryption. They involve a phished password, an approval tricked out of an accounts executive, a forwarding rule that quietly copies invoices to an outside address, or an ex-employee whose account was never closed. Against those, the controls that matter are enforced multi-factor authentication, sender authentication on your domain, forwarding restrictions and quick account recovery.

A second, rarer threat is the provider's own access to your data: staff access, legal requests, or a breach at the provider. Here the question is who holds the encryption keys. The sections below treat both threats separately.

## Encryption: in transit, at rest and who holds the keys

**In transit.** Mail is encrypted between your device and the provider, and between providers when both ends support TLS. No provider can promise this for every message, because the other side must cooperate. Check that your provider supports enforced TLS for partners you choose, and that old mail clients are not using unencrypted ports.

**At rest.** Microsoft 365, Google Workspace and Zoho encrypt stored mail on their servers as standard. This protects against stolen disks, not a hijacked account. Someone with your password and no second factor reads everything in plain text.

**Who holds the keys.** With the three mainstream providers, the provider manages the keys, which is what lets them offer server-side search, spam filtering, malware scanning and easy recovery. The trade-off is that the provider can technically access content, and is bound by law to respond to valid legal requests. Microsoft 365 adds document-level protection through sensitivity labels with encryption, so a protected file keeps its restrictions after it leaves your tenant. Higher tiers add customer-managed key options, which are positioned for larger organisations; ask what your edition includes.

**Proton** takes a different approach. Messages between Proton users are end-to-end encrypted, and stored mail uses zero-access encryption, meaning Proton does not hold the keys needed to read your mailbox. Mail to people outside Proton can be sent with a password-protected link. That is a real security advantage for sensitive work, such as a law firm, a clinic or a founder handling board papers. The cost is features: search over encrypted content works differently, there is no equivalent of the deep compliance tooling in an enterprise suite, and the collaboration ecosystem is smaller.

## Multi-factor authentication and passkeys

Ask three questions of any provider.

- Can the administrator enforce MFA for every user, or is it optional?
- Which second factors are allowed? An authenticator app, passkey or hardware key is stronger than an SMS code, which can be intercepted through SIM-swap fraud.
- Can access be conditional, for example blocking sign-ins from unmanaged devices or unusual locations?

Microsoft 365 offers basic enforcement across Business plans. Conditional access, which decides whether a sign-in is allowed based on device, location and risk, comes with Entra ID P1 inside [Business Premium](/products/microsoft-365-business-premium); our guide to [Business Premium security you already own](/blog/microsoft-365-business-premium-security-you-already-own) explains why it is the most valuable switch and so often left off. Google Workspace supports 2-Step Verification, including security keys and passkeys, which an administrator can require. Zoho lists two-factor authentication and admin policy control, so confirm enforcement options for your edition. Proton supports two-factor authentication and hardware keys for accounts.

## Phishing and spoofing defences: SPF, DKIM and DMARC

Three DNS records decide whether someone can send mail that appears to come from your domain.

- **SPF** lists the servers allowed to send for you.
- **DKIM** adds a signature the receiving server verifies.
- **DMARC** tells receivers what to do when those checks fail and sends you reports.

All four providers support publishing these for a custom domain. The work is yours: add the records at your DNS host, identify every legitimate sender (accounts software, CRM, website forms), then move DMARC from monitoring to enforcement. Large mailbox providers now expect these records from bulk senders, so skipping them also hurts delivery.

Inbound filtering differs by edition. Microsoft's advanced protection against malicious links and attachments sits in the Defender for Office 365 tier included with Business Premium, whereas Business Basic and Standard rely on standard filtering. Ask each provider what scanning is included in the plan you will actually buy.

## Admin controls and audit logs

A long feature list matters less than a short list you will configure. In a trial, look for:

- Instant sign-out and password reset for a single user
- Blocking of automatic forwarding to external addresses, organisation-wide
- Alerts on suspicious sign-ins and new mailbox rules
- Role-based admin access, so the person resetting passwords is not a full super-admin
- Mobile policy: PIN requirement and remote wipe of company data only
- Audit logs showing who signed in, who changed what, and who searched a mailbox, with a stated retention period

Microsoft 365 is the deepest on device control, with Intune in Business Premium; our comparison of [Business Standard and Business Premium](/blog/microsoft-365-business-standard-vs-business-premium) shows the difference. Google Workspace and Zoho are generally simpler to run. Proton for Business has an admin console for users, domains and policies, but is lighter than the large suites on device management, rules and reporting. A configured console on a basic plan beats an unconfigured one on a premium plan.

## Data residency, the DPDP Act and compliance

Data residency is more nuanced than "is it in India?". Ask every provider in writing where mailbox data, backups, search indexes and attachments sit, whether the location can be pinned, which support staff can reach the data, and whether the commitment is contractual. Several large providers operate data centres in India, with commitments that vary by product and edition. Proton is headquartered in Switzerland and has historically hosted data there, so it is not an India-resident option; whether that matters depends on your contracts.

In general terms, India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 expects organisations that handle personal data to apply reasonable security safeguards and to deal properly with personal data breaches. Email is a place where customer and employee personal data accumulates. The Act does not name an email product, and it does not make any one provider compliant for you. Your obligations depend on your role and sector, so take advice from your compliance adviser.

For assurance reports and certifications, ask each provider for its current published documents, and request them under confidentiality if needed. Do not treat a logo on a web page as an audit.

## Recovery, backup and retention

Mail that can be deleted by a compromised account, or by a mistake, is not safe. Check retention and recovery separately.

- **Deleted item recovery:** how long deleted mail stays recoverable, and by whom.
- **Retention and eDiscovery:** keeping mail for a set period regardless of user deletion, and searching it for an investigation. Microsoft 365 Business plans cover everyday mail, with deeper compliance tooling positioned in Enterprise plans such as [Microsoft 365 E3](/products/microsoft-365-e3). Zoho lists retention and eDiscovery on higher editions. Google offers its Vault tool on certain editions.
- **Independent backup:** a copy outside the provider's own platform protects against deletion, ransomware and account takeover. Proton's zero-access design makes server-side recovery and search different from other providers, so plan your own export routine.

If a regulator, bank or court could ask for a former employee's mail from three years ago, this section decides your edition, not the headline price.

## Comparison table

| Security point | Microsoft 365 | Google Workspace | Zoho | Proton |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Encryption in transit and at rest | Standard | Standard | Standard | Standard, plus end-to-end between Proton users |
| Who holds mailbox keys | Provider by default | Provider by default | Provider by default | User (zero-access) |
| Document-level protection | Sensitivity labels with encryption | Check by edition | Check by edition | Password-protected messages to outsiders |
| MFA enforcement | Yes; conditional access in Business Premium | Yes; security keys and passkeys | Listed; confirm per edition | Two-factor and hardware keys |
| SPF, DKIM, DMARC | Supported | Supported | Supported | Supported on custom domains |
| Device management | Intune in Business Premium | Check by edition | Check by edition | Limited |
| Retention and eDiscovery | Strongest on Enterprise plans | Vault on certain editions | Higher editions | Limited by design |
| Collaboration depth | Highest, native Office desktop apps | Browser-first | Moderate | Smaller ecosystem |

The table is a starting point for questions, not a verdict. Fill it in with your own trial findings.

## What it costs, in context

Price should be the last filter, because the security gap between editions inside one provider is usually larger than the gap between providers.

- [Zoho Mail](/products/zoho-mail) starts at {{price:zoho-mail}} per user per year excluding GST, and [Zoho Workplace](/products/zoho-workplace), which adds documents, storage, chat and meetings, starts at {{price:zoho-workplace}}.
- Microsoft 365 Business Basic is {{price:microsoft-365-business-basic}} per user per year, Business Standard is {{price:microsoft-365-business-standard}}, and Business Premium is {{price:microsoft-365-business-premium}}, all excluding GST.
- For Google Workspace and Proton, get current pricing from the providers; we do not quote them.

Prices are annual and tentative, and a written quotation fixes the final figure. GST at 18% is added on the invoice and is usually claimable as input credit by GST-registered buyers.

## Which to choose

- **Choose Microsoft 365 Business Premium** if staff use personal phones for work mail, you must show an auditor or customer that access is controlled, or you already run Windows laptops and Microsoft tools.
- **Choose Microsoft 365 Business Standard** for desktop Office needs with a modest risk profile, and enforce MFA anyway.
- **Choose Google Workspace** if your team lives in browser documents, you have no dedicated IT person, and simple administration beats deep device control.
- **Choose Zoho Mail or Workplace** if cost control matters and you mainly need domain email with sensible policies.
- **Choose Proton** for a small team or a few individuals who handle highly confidential material and can live without deep admin tooling and compliance search. Some businesses use it for a handful of sensitive mailboxes only.
- **Do not run two platforms** half-migrated: two credentials, two consoles and twice the attack surface.

For the wider productivity comparison, see [Microsoft 365 versus Google Workspace for Indian SMEs](/blog/microsoft-365-versus-google-workspace-for-indian-smes).

## A 30-minute trial audit

1. Enforce MFA for all test users and try signing in without it.
2. Block external auto-forwarding and test that the block works.
3. Publish SPF, DKIM and DMARC for a test domain and send to an outside address.
4. Enrol a phone and try the remote wipe.
5. Search a mailbox as an administrator and check that the action is logged.
6. Delete a message, then recover it.

## Moving safely

Migration is where mail gets lost or exposed: forwarding left on, old accounts left active, DNS records changed in the wrong order. We advise on [email migration](/services/email-migration) and [Microsoft 365 deployment](/services/microsoft-365), including security settings from day one. We supply Microsoft 365 and Zoho, and we will say plainly if Google Workspace or Proton suits you better; for those we advise only and do not resell them. See the [Microsoft 365 plans](/microsoft-365) or [request a quotation](/enquiry).

faqs.question: Which is the most secure business email provider in India?
faqs.answer: None is best for every company. For stolen passwords and spoofing, the winner is whichever you configure fully, with enforced MFA, DMARC and forwarding limits. For protection from the provider itself, Proton's zero-access design is strongest, at the cost of collaboration and admin features.

faqs.question: Is Proton Mail suitable for a whole company?
faqs.answer: It can suit small teams handling confidential material. Its trade-offs are lighter device management, limited compliance search by design and a smaller collaboration ecosystem than Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace. Larger teams often keep a mainstream suite and use Proton for a few sensitive mailboxes.

faqs.question: Do SPF, DKIM and DMARC protect my inbox?
faqs.answer: They mainly protect your domain and customers by making it harder to send mail that appears to come from you. They also improve delivery. Publish all three, then move DMARC to enforcement once every legitimate sender is listed.

faqs.question: Does the DPDP Act require a particular email provider?
faqs.answer: No. The Act is general about reasonable security safeguards and breach handling for personal data and does not name a product. Whether a provider supports your obligations depends on your role, sector and contracts, so ask your compliance adviser.

faqs.question: Is my business email stored in India?
faqs.answer: It depends on the provider, product and contract. Ask in writing where mailboxes, backups and search indexes sit, who can access them, and whether the commitment is contractual. Proton is Swiss-based, so it is not an India-resident option.

faqs.question: Does TechZoid sell Google Workspace or Proton?
faqs.answer: No. We supply Microsoft 365 and Zoho Mail and Workplace. For Google Workspace or Proton we advise on choice and migration only, and we will say if one of them fits you better than what we sell.
